title: Local Proj comparison under restrictions and degreewise units
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{k\geq0}\mathcal A_k$ and $\mathcal B=\bigoplus_{k\geq0}\mathcal B_k$ be commutative unital graded $\mathcal O_S$-algebra sheaves, quasi-coherent as $\mathcal O_S$-modules [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures; def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Put $P_{\mathcal A}=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal A)$ and $P_{\mathcal B}=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal B)$, with their structure maps and specified affine restriction isomorphisms $i_U$ [def-nagata-relative-proj]. Let $U\subseteq S$ be affine and let $\beta:\mathcal A|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B|_U$ be a graded $\mathcal O_U$-algebra isomorphism. There is a unique $U$-isomorphism $r_{\beta,U}:P_{\mathcal B}|_U\to P_{\mathcal A}|_U$ with the following chart description. With $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal A)$ and $B=\Gamma(U,\mathcal B)$, for every $f\in A_d$, $d>0$, its inverse image of $D_+(f)$ is $D_+(\beta(f))$, and, under $i_U$ and the standard affine chart identifications, its ring map is
$$A_{(f),0}\longrightarrow B_{(\beta(f)),0},\qquad a/f^m\longmapsto\beta(a)/\beta(f)^m\quad(a\in A_{md}).$$
Here the chart rings are the degree-zero homogeneous localizations [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero] and a chart map means the induced spectrum morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. These inverse-image charts cover $P_{\mathcal B}|_U$. The inverse of $r_{\beta,U}$ is $r_{\beta^{-1},U}$. For every affine $V\subseteq U$, restriction over $V$ identifies $r_{\beta,U}|_V$ with $r_{\beta|_V,V}$, also for the inverse maps; on a chart coefficient restriction $\rho$ sends $\beta(a)/\beta(f)^m$ to $\rho\beta(a)/\rho\beta(f)^m$.
If $u\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_S)^\times$ and $\beta'$ is another graded $\mathcal O_U$-algebra isomorphism such that $\beta'|_{\mathcal A_k}=u^k\beta|_{\mathcal A_k}$ for every $k\geq0$, then $r_{\beta',U}=r_{\beta,U}$, including equality of their inverses. On the common chart $D_+(\beta'(f))=D_+(\beta(f))$, the equality of the two chart maps is the equality
$$\frac{\beta'(a)}{\beta'(f)^m}=\frac{u^{md}\beta(a)}{(u^d\beta(f))^m}=\frac{\beta(a)}{\beta(f)^m}\quad(a\in A_{md}).$$
No regularity or non-zero-divisor condition on $f$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_S)$. The specified $i_U$ identify the two relative restrictions with $\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ and $\operatorname{Proj}(B)$ [def-nagata-relative-proj]. On sections $\beta$ is a graded $R$-algebra isomorphism. Apply [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] with the identity $R\to R$ and the graded isomorphism $R\otimes_R A\to B$, $r\otimes a\mapsto r\beta(a)$. Its inverse is $b\mapsto1\otimes\beta^{-1}(b)$: the balanced-tensor relation $r\otimes a=1\otimes ra$ verifies both composites. The induced $\psi$ is exactly $\beta$. That node supplies the morphism over $U$, the inverse-image charts, the stated fraction formula, their covering, and uniqueness. Conjugating with the specified $i_U$ gives $r_{\beta,U}$. No equality $\mathcal A_0=\mathcal O_U$ is used.

source.place: Tags 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), 01N2 (lemma-base-change-map-proj), specialization to identity scalar extension

proof.text: Perform step 1 with $\beta^{-1}$. On the chart indexed by $f\in A_d$, the composite ring map sends $a/f^m$ first to $\beta(a)/\beta(f)^m$ and then to $a/f^m$. In the other order the same calculation starts with any positive-degree homogeneous $g\in B$ and sends $b/g^m$ back to itself. These fractions exhaust the chart rings [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. Spectrum functoriality [def-weil-affine-spectrum] therefore makes both scheme composites identities on their charts. The charts cover by step 1; uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] makes both composites identities globally. Thus $r_{\beta,U}^{-1}=r_{\beta^{-1},U}$, and the uniqueness already proved for the morphism gives the asserted unique $U$-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), chart formula applied to inverse graded isomorphisms

proof.text:
For affine $V\subseteq U$, write $\rho_A:A\to A_V$ and $\rho_B:B\to B_V$ for restriction. The compatibility data in [def-nagata-relative-proj] identify $P_{\mathcal A}|_V\to P_{\mathcal A}|_U$ and its $\mathcal B$ counterpart with these coefficient restriction maps on localized charts. Sheaf naturality gives $\rho_B\beta=\beta_V\rho_A$, where $\beta_V=\Gamma(V,\beta|_V)$. The two composites from $P_{\mathcal B}|_V$ to $P_{\mathcal A}|_U$ have inverse image of $D_+(f)$ equal to $D_+(\rho_B\beta(f))=D_+(\beta_V\rho_A(f))$, by step 1 and the specified restriction charts. Their chart comorphisms agree, since
$$\frac{a}{f^m}\longmapsto\frac{\rho_B\beta(a)}{\rho_B\beta(f)^m}=\frac{\beta_V\rho_A(a)}{\beta_V\rho_A(f)^m}.$$
The inverse images of the step-1 chart cover still cover after restriction to $V$. Spectrum functoriality and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] give equality of the composites, hence the required equality over $V$ under $i_V$. This also proves the specified formula for coefficient restriction. Apply this same argument to $\beta^{-1}$ to obtain compatibility of the inverse maps.

source.place: Tags 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), 01N2 (lemma-base-change-map-proj); specified affine restriction compatibility in relative Proj

proof.text:
Write $v$ for the image of $u$ in $B_0$; it is a unit with inverse the image of $u^{-1}$. For $f\in A_d$, membership of $v^d\beta(f)$ in a homogeneous prime is equivalent to membership of $\beta(f)$, so their standard opens coincide. Their canonical chart-ring identification is
$$B_{(v^d\beta(f)),0}\longrightarrow B_{(\beta(f)),0},\qquad \frac{b}{(v^d\beta(f))^m}\longmapsto\frac{v^{-dm}b}{\beta(f)^m}.$$
Its inverse multiplies the numerator by $v^{dm}$; both formulas respect the ordinary localization relation and preserve degree zero [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. Under this identification the chart formula from step 1 for $\beta'$ sends $a/f^m$, $a\in A_{md}$, to
$$\frac{v^{-dm}\beta'(a)}{\beta(f)^m}=\frac{v^{-dm}v^{md}\beta(a)}{\beta(f)^m}=\frac{\beta(a)}{\beta(f)^m}.$$
Thus the two spectrum morphisms agree on every chart [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and the covering and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] give $r_{\beta',U}=r_{\beta,U}$. Equality of inverses follows by composing this equality with the two inverses. Only the unit $v$ was cancelled; neither $f$ nor $\beta(f)$ was cancelled, so no non-zero-divisor hypothesis is needed.
